scenes.heading: Data Engineer vs Data Scientist
scenes.narration: Data engineers and data scientists are close collaborators, yet their goals and daily work differ sharply.

scenes.heading: Different goals
bullets: Engineers deliver clean, reliable data at scale
Scientists build models and extract predictions
scenes.narration: Engineers aim to deliver clean data reliably because models are only as good as the data feeding them. Scientists aim to build models that predict or classify, turning that data into foresight. Engineers spend their effort tuning pipelines and storage, whereas scientists spend theirs tuning algorithms and improving accuracy. The two priorities complement one another.

scenes.heading: Focus and skills
scenes.narration: The engineer brings a software engineering mindset centered on reliable, scalable systems. The scientist brings a research mindset centered on statistics and experimentation. A data scientist's models cannot run without the trustworthy data pipelines an engineer provides.

scenes.heading: From raw data to prediction
scenes.narration: The engineer first prepares clean, well-structured data for use. The scientist then trains a model on that data and validates its predictions. Finally the engineer helps operationalize the model in a production pipeline so it runs continuously.

scenes.text: Engineers make data usable; scientists make data predictive. Great analytics needs both.
scenes.narration: The simplest distinction is that engineers make data usable while scientists make it predictive, and strong teams rely on both working in concert.
